pose_summary.legal_basis: legal = the board is clean at this pose; no_worse = the verdict this verb refuses on (relative to the input board)

pad_legality.oob_pad_copper_basis: per-PAD copper rects against the real outline at margin 0 (the authoritative measure; the same question render_placement answers in checklist.a_off_outline.pad_copper)
pad_legality.oob_pad_basis: part pad AABB vs outline inflated by the grading clearance (NOT the per-pad outline measure; see render_placement checklist.a_off_outline.pad_copper)

check_assembly.coincident_origins_basis: every footprint BLOCK (#726): blocks sharing one reference are keyed with an ordinal suffix, so they form a pair here like any other two parts. See duplicate_references for the names the board itself uses.
check_assembly.oob_pad_basis: part pad AABB vs outline inflated by the grading clearance (NOT the per-pad outline measure; see render_placement checklist.a_off_outline.pad_copper)
check_assembly.oob_pad_copper_basis: per-PAD copper rects against the real outline at margin 0 (the authoritative measure; the same question render_placement answers in checklist.a_off_outline.pad_copper)
check_assembly.parts_by_side_basis: every footprint BLOCK (#726): blocks sharing one reference are keyed with an ordinal suffix and counted separately. `pad_bearing` restricts that to blocks carrying at least one pad, and it is the count the populated-side verdict is taken from -- a zero-pad graphic on the back does not make a board double-sided.
